newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada churches give 9,000 tonnes food to Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Canada churches give 9,000 tonnes food to Rwanda.

text.p: A Canadian church group said on Monday it began to ship the first of 9,000 tonnes in donated food to Rwandan refugees.
"There's a thousand tonnes in place now. The volume could go up after our board meeting in December and if the partners decide to give more," Canadian Foodgrains Bank spokeswoman Trish Jordan said.

The Winnipeg-based agency represents 13 Christian church groups and takes donations of grains and oilseeds from Canadian farmers. The agency focused on Rwanda's refugees and the malnourished of North Korea, Afghanistan and Liberia.
Varying quantities of grain, lentils and oilseeds will be shipped to Rwanda's refugees via Kigali between now and May.
The Canadian International Development Agency, a government body, however, did not plan to add to the food aid.
"The NGOs (non-governmental organizations) in the region have the supplies they need. It has not yet received our attention," CIDA spokesman Andre Desrosiers said.
Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale committed Canada last week at the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization summit to donate 400,000 tonnes of food aid in the current fiscal year.
